candidates.attacker_control: A raw TCP client fully controls the OpenWire command type byte (e.g., 31 = EXCEPTION_RESPONSE, CommandTypes.java lines 84-85), the 'has throwable' boolean, and the class-name and message strings parsed by tightUnmarsalThrowable/looseUnmarsalThrowable. The type byte is used to index dataMarshallers in OpenWireFormat.doUnmarshal (lines 343-362) with no sender/state check.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) Class.forName is called with initialize=false; however, Constructor.newInstance still triggers class initialization and runs the String constructor, and only then does the (Throwable) cast fail, with the exception caught at lines 232-234, so non-Throwable classes still execute their side effects. (2) No Throwable.class.isAssignableFrom or allow-list check exists in any of the v1..v10 / legacy v2..v8 copies (searched for isAssignableFrom and Throwable.class.isAssignableFrom; zero matches). (3) The sink is not restricted to post-auth clients: unmarshalling occurs in the TcpTransport read loop before TransportConnection.service (TransportConnection.java lines 180-198, 326-375), so no credentials or prior WireFormatInfo are needed to reach it. (4) Both tightEncodingEnabled=true and false paths end in the same createThrowable call, so the encoding negotiated does not change the outcome. (5) The class must be present on the broker classpath, and successful RCE depends on the presence of a gadget constructor, which is deployment-specific; the standard assembly does ship Spring/other libraries. (6) No code was executed and no exploit was attempted; all claims are source-level.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote attacker can cause the broker JVM to load and instantiate arbitrary classes available on its classpath with attacker-chosen String constructor arguments, before any broker-level authentication or authorization. With a suitable side-effecting class present (standard distributions bundle Spring and other libraries), this class-instantiation primitive can lead to remote code execution; even without a full RCE gadget it yields arbitrary side effects from constructors/static initializers and can be abused for denial of service. The same primitive is reachable from multiple command types and all supported protocol versions, so version negotiation or switching command types does not mitigate it.
candidates.prerequisites: Network reachability to an OpenWire connector; the shipped default configuration exposes openwire at tcp://0.0.0.0:61616 (assembly/src/release/conf/activemq.xml lines 111-118) with no authentication plugin, and the vulnerable sink is in the transport read loop, so it triggers before the broker's authentication/authorization or service() handling. A class with a public String constructor and dangerous side effects must exist on the broker classpath; the shipped binary assembly includes Spring libraries (assembly/src/main/descriptors/common-bin.xml lines 186-190; activemq-spring/pom.xml line 59), which historically supply such side-effecting constructors.
candidates.root_cause: BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable() takes the throwable class name and message directly from the OpenWire byte stream and executes Class.forName(className, false, loader), clazz.getConstructor(String.class) and constructor.newInstance(message) without verifying Throwable.class.isAssignableFrom(clazz) and without any allow-list. The returned object is cast to Throwable only after the constructor call, so a non-Throwable gadget class still runs its constructor/static initialization and the resulting ClassCastException is silently swallowed by the catch (Throwable e) branch. The same duplicated sink exists in every wire-format version (activemq-client v1..v10 and activemq-openwire-legacy v2..v8), and is invoked for the Throwable fields of ExceptionResponse, ConnectionError and MessageAck.poisonCause via tightUnmarsalThrowable/looseUnmarsalThrowable.
candidates.title: Pre-auth arbitrary class instantiation via OpenWire throwable unmarshalling (createThrowable)
candidates.trace: TCP socket data -> TcpTransport.run/doRun/readCommand (TcpTransport.java 191-222) -> OpenWireFormat.unmarshal (OpenWireFormat.java 176-198 / 255-269) -> doUnmarshal (343-362) -> v10 ExceptionResponseMarshaller.tightUnmarshal or looseUnmarshal (ExceptionResponseMarshaller.java 65-71 / 109-115; same for ConnectionErrorMarshaller and MessageAckMarshaller) -> BaseDataStreamMarshaller.tightUnmarsalThrowable / looseUnmarsalThrowable (BaseDataStreamMarshaller.java 187-225 / 508-546) -> createThrowable (227-235): Class.forName(attackerClass) + getConstructor(String.class) + newInstance(attackerMessage).
candidates.unverified: End-to-end remote code execution was not verified at runtime and depends on a suitable attacker-usable String-constructor class being on the deployment classpath; I did not enumerate the full runtime classpath, only the assembly descriptors that bundle Spring and related libraries. The exact default tight/loose encoding state of the server-side OpenWireFormat before WireFormatInfo negotiation was inferred from field defaults and negotiate logic, not observed; both states reach the same sink, so this does not change the finding.
candidates.weakness_type: Unsafe reflection / attacker-controlled class instantiation during deserialization (untrusted data in Class.forName + Constructor.newInstance)

coverage_summary: Source scope reported 2446 model-visible files; only binary-like files are skipped by the read/search tools and no other path filters applied. I reviewed in full or in part: the OpenWire client marshalling stack (v1..v10 BaseDataStreamMarshaller/createThrowable, ExceptionResponse/ConnectionError/MessageAck marshallers, MarshallerFactory, OpenWireFormat, OpenWireFormatFactory, CommandTypes), the legacy v2..v8 marshallers, the TCP transport read path (TcpTransport/TcpTransportServer/TransportFactory), the broker TransportConnection service/dispatch path, default shipped configuration (assembly/src/release/conf/activemq.xml, jetty.xml, activemq-fileserver web.xml, common-bin.xml), the ObjectMessage deserialization path (ActiveMQObjectMessage, ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream, ObjectStreamWireFormat), and the web/web-console module listings. I did not exhaustively review the broker region/store/network-bridge code, other protocol implementations (STOMP, MQTT, AMQP, WS), JAAS, console, pools, or the full web console Java/JS code.
limitations: No code was executed, no tests/scanners were run, and no exploit was attempted; the finding is a source-level lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

Successful code-execution impact depends on a side-effecting class with a public String constructor being present on the deployment classpath; the assembly descriptor shows Spring libraries are bundled in the standard distribution, but I did not enumerate the complete runtime classpath.

The server-side OpenWireFormat's initial tight/loose encoding mode before WireFormatInfo negotiation was reasoned from field defaults and renegotiateWireFormat logic rather than observed; both modes share the same vulnerable sink, so this does not affect the finding's existence.

The 2446-file snapshot was not reviewed exhaustively; many broker, persistence, network and non-OpenWire protocol files were not inspected, so additional vulnerabilities may exist that are not covered here.
Two binary-like files were skipped by the tooling; they were not inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: Java native deserialization of ObjectMessage content (ClassLoadingAwareObjectInputStream has no class allow-list; ActiveMQObjectMessage.getObject() lines 180-195; ObjectStreamWireFormat.unmarshal lines 59-66)
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible CVE-2015-5254-style lead, but the broker does not deserialize message bodies on ingest; exploitation requires a victim consumer, a broker-side logger, or the web console to call getObject()/toString() on a crafted object message. That extra second-stage condition and the weaker pre-auth story made it less strong than the OpenWire sink; not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Unauthenticated HTTP PUT file upload via the /fileserver webapp (activemq-fileserver web.xml maps Jetty DefaultServlet at /*; assembly/src/release/conf/jetty.xml security constraints cover only /api/*, /admin/*, *.jsp while /fileserver is mounted unprotected; RestFilter.doPut writes files)
rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking CVE-2016-3088-style lead, but exploitability depends on the bundled external Jetty DefaultServlet PUT semantics and on a writable/executable webapp directory, which cannot be confirmed from this source tree alone (the Jetty implementation is a dependency, not in-repo). Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: JMX management surface (ManagementContext, AnnotatedMBean, Log4JConfigView) possibly exposed without authentication
rejected_leads.reason: Not inspected in depth; no source evidence of a concrete attacker-controlled path/impact was gathered, so it was not promoted.

summary: Repository is an Apache ActiveMQ 5.11.0 source snapshot (root pom.xml line 28). I reviewed the OpenWire protocol marshalling/unmarshalling stack, the broker's transport ingress, the default shipped broker/web configuration, and spot-checked the ObjectMessage and fileserver paths. The strongest, best source-evidenced candidate is the pre-authentication unsafe-reflection sink in OpenWire throwable unmarshalling (BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable): an attacker-controlled class name read off the wire is passed to Class.forName/getConstructor/newInstance with no Throwable/allow-list check. Because the (Throwable) cast happens only after the constructor has already run, any class with a public String constructor available on the broker classpath is instantiated, and the ClassCastException is swallowed by the surrounding catch. The path is reached during socket-read unmarshalling, before the broker's service()/security processing, on the default OpenWire connector. This is a candidate lead, not a runtime-confirmed exploit; RCE pivoting depends on a suitable gadget class being on the deployment classpath (the binary assembly bundles Spring libraries, which historically provide such constructors).
